_about: The Meghna system (Stage 2, batch b3): the Meghna — a card, drawn as two main lines, the new upper stretch from where OSM names it (near Austagram) to Bhairab and the pinned line on to 22.38°N — the Barak, Surma and Kushiyara, and the Titas; those four in the `disputed` role, because the two books give them different roles. Left out: the Kalni (OSM has no Kalni below Ajmiriganj, where it tags the stream Kushiyara; only two fragments in Sunamganj). Research: tools/.cache/bangladesh-rivers/research4-b3.md (quote ids B3-…) and osm-b3/ways.md.

meghnaUpper.identified: Five ways from the pinned rivers snapshot (key meghna), every link sharing a node, tagged «মেঘনা নদী» / Meghna River, all in relation 11130102 (Q1125242): from where OSM first names the Meghna (node 13911810185, on the unnamed Kushiyara-relation way 674084134, in Nasirnagar near Austagram) to node 3601495737 at Bhairab, the first node of way 1076997905, where the pinned line `meghna` begins. Not drawn: six side channels near Sonargaon/Gazaria, and 674084134 (unnamed).

meghna.identified: One chain of ten OSM ways named «মেঘনা নদী» (name:en «Meghna River») from the Meghna above Bhairab Bazar, where the Old Brahmaputra joins it (the book), past the Padma junction, to 22.3835°N. Ways 630320743 and 908091551 carry a name:bn tag reading «গঙ্গা নদী» in OSM; their name and position are the Meghna's. The picture stops at 22.38°N, above the estuary. From Stage 2 (b3) a main line of the Meghna's card, no longer a grey continuation; its ways, and so its geometry pin, are unchanged.

join.source: OSM node 306476755, the last node of way 44882516, where the Surma and the Kushiyara both begin (Zakiganj)

barak.identified: Three ways tagged "Barāk River" / Barak River (relation 5904028, Q1709169; this batch's extract), from beyond the frame's east edge to node 306476755 at Zakiganj, where OSM's Surma and Kushiyara begin. All but the last node lie in India (COD-AB): drawn dashed. The relation continues upstream into Manipur, outside the frame; not drawn.

surma.identified: Seven ways from the pinned rivers snapshot (key surma), every link sharing a node, all in relation 5904030 (Q2985860) as main_stream: from the Barak's end node at Zakiganj to Nikli, where OSM's Ghorautra begins; no stretch below is named Surma. A connector (10.2 km) joins its end to the Meghna (ⓘ). 644709637 is kept as pinned (current OSM differs by at most 6 m).

kushiyara.identified: Eight ways from the pinned rivers snapshot (key kushiyara), every link sharing a node, all in relation 5904029 (Q3347200) as main_stream: from the Barak's end node at Zakiganj to Austagram. A connector (9.8 km) joins its end to the Meghna (ⓘ); OSM's only link, the unnamed relation member 674084134, runs on 13.3 km beside the Meghna as a second channel, so it is not drawn.

join.source: OSM node 4242523054, the end of way 424888079 on the Meghna's way 685430035 (node 8), in Sarail

titas.identified: Three ways tagged "Titas River" (this batch's extract): from the Meghna at Sarail (424888079), on 484348101 from its node 2 (4770917200, where 424888079 meets it; its first 1 km, a spur, is trimmed), to 608406115's dead end near Brahmanbaria town. Not drawn: two side channels (608414930 and 174635641, the latter tagged «তিতাস নদী», Nabinagar–Akhaura), whose ends lie 7.3 and 10.4 km from anything drawn.

entities.review: The card is the Meghna as both books' «মেঘনা» paragraphs give it, from the Barak in Assam. Tributaries and distributaries are null: the same four rivers (Manu, Baulai, Titas, Gumti) are «উপনদী» in B-GEO and «শাখা নদী» in B910 (ⓘ). Length is null, as the Jamuna's and the Padma's: BWDB gives two reaches, SE-17 «মেঘনা (আপার)» 156 km and SE-18 «মেঘনা (লোয়ার)» 65 km, never summed; en WP 140 and 130 km (ⓘ). Where the name begins: both books below Ajmiriganj, after the Kalni; BWDB starts SE-17 at Lakhai, Habiganj (ⓘ). BWDB's reach names «মেঘনা (আপার)» and «মেঘনা (লোয়ার)» are not on the card; SE-18's local name «মেমানিয়া» is. The drawn line begins where OSM first names the Meghna, near Austagram, and ends 1.5 km short of COD-AB's coast.

entities.review: Both books open the Meghna paragraph with the Barak, its source river in Assam. Relation, entry and end are null: B-GEO has it divide into the Surma and the Kushiyara before entering Sylhet, B910 has it join Sylhet's Surma and Kushiyara (ⓘ); BWDB, JRCB's Kushiyara brief and OSM draw a fork at Zakiganj. Course: MISSING (the books give only «আসামের»). JRCB puts its source in «মিজোরাম, মনিপুর» (ⓘ). No BWDB entry: NE-96 «শাখা বরাক» is a small river in Nabiganj, ruled out.
